limber

LIM-ber · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Limber is capable of bending or being shaped easily; physically flexible.

The physical therapist showed her patients a five-minute routine designed to keep their hips limber well into old age.

Worked Example

Before every game, the team spent fifteen minutes on dynamic stretches to keep their hamstrings limber and reduce the risk of pulling a muscle.

Being able to stretch and bend easily without strain, especially after preparation like warming up, is exactly what limber describes.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

loose: Loose describes muscles that are relaxed and free of tightness at this moment, usually right after warming up. Limber names a lasting ability: a limber body can bend and stretch through its whole range without strain. Your shoulders can feel loose today while your body stays far from limber.

elastic: Elastic describes material that stretches and then snaps back into shape, like a rubber band or a waistband. Limber is for living bodies: joints and muscles that bend easily without strain. Calling a runner limber praises her flexibility; calling something elastic just describes what it is made of.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

stiff: difficult to bend or move

rigid: unable to bend; completely inflexible

Where it sits · how easily the body bends — flexible → limber → supple

flexible vs. limber: Flexible is milder than limber: almost anything that bends a little counts as flexible, even a plastic ruler, while a limber body bends easily and comfortably through stretches that would strain most people.

supple vs. limber: Supple is stronger than limber: a limber body bends easily after a good stretch, while a supple spine, trained by years of dance, arches backward until the palms touch the floor.

The pieces

Put it together

Put it together: Limber has been in English since the 1560s, but its exact origin is uncertain. One guess connects it to limb, picturing something that moves as loosely as a tree branch swaying in the wind.
